picks.blurb: TCU vs Texas Tech Score Predictions From the KillerFrogs Staff Skip to main content SI.COM Frogs in the Pros FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS SI.COM FROGS FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM FROGS BB MEM'RIES SWEET TCU was unable to capture a win in its home finale against #2 Utah, losing 38-17. However, the Horned Frogs will get one more shot at becoming bowl-eligible on Thanksgiving Day against the No. 9-ranked Texas Tech Red Raiders. With Sonny Dykes no longer serving as the head coach of the Frogs, interim head coach Andy Avalos will be tasked with attempting to upset Texas Tech in Lubbock. Kickoff is set for 7 p.m. CT on ESPN. The Horned Frogs enter the game at 5-6 overall and 3-5 in the Big 12. Texas Tech is 10-1 and 7-1 in conference play. If TCU pulls off the big upset on Thursday, they will become bowl-eligible. Otherwise, the Frogs' season will be over. Either way, the Frogs will have changes coming their way. Texas Tech had a narrow win last week, as Baylor took the Red Raiders to the wire before they came out on top, 20-10. If the Frogs can make Texas Tech QB Thomas Castellanos uncomfortable like Baylor did, I like the Frogs' odds. Texas Tech has also struggled with consistency this season. However, the Frogs will have their hands full if they let him dictate where the ball goes. As I wrote in my Utah report card , the Frogs have quite a bit to fix, but I truly believe they will be playing hard for Andy Avalos in the regular-season finale. Can the Horned Frogs protect the football, play hard, and bring the energy? Here’s how the KillerFrogs staff sees the regular-season finale. Michael Bara V believes the rivalry and the interim coaching change will bring out something special in the Frogs. He expects the defense to rally behind Andy Avalos and help TCU pull off the upset. Aiden Reed sees TCU eliminating Texas Tech from Big 12 contention, assuming BYU wins, as the Frogs take advantage of having nothing to lose and fighting for bowl eligibility. He also expects TCU to pull off its annual Thanksgiving upset. Baileigh Sheffield expects the Frogs to keep things competitive early, but sees Texas Tech pulling away in the second half for a two-touchdown victory. Jackson James is counting on history repeating itself, pointing to TCU's upset of an in-state rival after its last coaching change in 2021. He’s counting on the defense to hold up as it has all season and help TCU pull off the upset. As for me, I have been saying all season long that the Frogs would upset Texas Tech, and I'm sticking to that prediction. I believe this team has one more fight left in it, and I expect TCU to rise to the occasion in Andy Avalos' first game as interim head coach. My TCU vs. Texas Tech prediction backs the Horned Frogs +14.5, given the Red Raiders' red-zone struggles despite their overall statistical edge. The TCU Horned Frogs (5-6, 3-5 Big 12) visit the No. 9 Texas Tech Red Raiders (10-1, 7-1) in Week 13's Battle for the Saddle on Thursday, Nov. 26, at Jones AT&T Stadium in Lubbock, Texas (8 p.m. ET, ESPN). Kalshi lists Texas Tech as a 14.5-point favorite, with a total of 47.5 points and moneyline probabilities of 87% for Texas Tech and 16% for TCU. I'm fading the double-digit favorite in my college football picks . Spread prediction: TCU Horned Frogs +14.5 Total prediction: Under 47.5 TOP PICK TCU vs Texas Tech spread prediction: TCU +14.5 I'm fading the move toward the Texas Tech Red Raiders now that the spread has crossed a key number. I'll take TCU Horned Frogs +14.5, down to +12.5 . The Red Raiders opened as 10.5-point favorites at Kalshi. However, the line movement feels driven more by perception than new information . TCU firing Sonny Dykes this week is a new development, but Texas Tech's statistical edge and the Horned Frogs' absence of starting quarterback Jaden Craig were already factored into the opening line . More importantly, the Red Raiders rank 77th nationally in third-down conversion rate and 108th in red-zone scoring rate . That's a problem when laying nearly two touchdowns because converting in high-leverage situations is how favorites build a margin. TCU vs Texas Tech Over/Under pick: Under 47.5 The Under 47.5 is tradable down to 45.5 . Texas Tech can overwhelm TCU, so the Horned Frogs need to turn this game into a rock fight to have any shot at an upset. The Red Raiders have the 16th-highest rushing rate in the country, and TCU's defense ranks 18th in yards per rush allowed . The Horned Frogs also have the third-best red-zone defense nationally, which could compound Texas Tech's struggles in high-leverage situations and force the Red Raiders to settle for field goals. Meanwhile, both offensive lines struggle with pass protection and both defenses have high sack rates, opening the door for drive-killing sacks. TCU vs Texas Tech combo I'm essentially investing in Texas Tech winning ugly, which wouldn't be the worst outcome for a team with legitimate College Football Playoff hopes. If TCU can avoid giving the Red Raiders short fields, Texas Tech might have to chew up a significant amount of clock to build a comfortable lead. Furthermore, a two-score deficit wouldn't necessarily force the Horned Frogs to abandon their offensive game plan early, especially if their defense is keeping them within striking distance. picks.blurb: Will Texas Tech football punch its Big 12 title ticket vs TCU? Score prediction - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football CFP And Bowl Games Steelers release Aaron Rodgers NBA Cup roundup Latest CFP rankings MLB free agency updates Viral Ga. Tech couple Will Texas Tech football punch its Big 12 title ticket vs TCU? Score prediction Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The regular season comes to an end in Galaxy Stadium for the Texas Tech football team , with TCU coming to town for a Thanksgiving showdown under the lights. There's a lot going on here, but we'll begin with TCU, which will have a new coach running things and a new quarterback running the show. Well, not entirely new. Adam Schobel took the reins against Utah after starter Jaden Craig missed the game due to injury. TCU has already ruled Craig out for this week's game, so Schobel will take snaps and try to lead the upset over Texas Tech. The 6-foot-5 sophomore had one pass attempt this season before going 15-of-31 for 106 yards and throwing two interceptions against the Utes. But this game is less about matchups and more about what's on the line. What's at stake for Texas Tech football Things are pretty simple for the Red Raiders this week. Beat the Horned Frogs and they're heading back to AT&T Stadium on Dec. 4 for the Big 12 Conference championship game against Utah, which has already clinched a spot in the title encounter. A loss to TCU does two things. First, it makes Texas Tech wait another two days to figure out if it's heading to Arlington, needing BYU to lose to Cincinnati. Second, no win over TCU and no BYU loss means Tech can pretty much kiss its College Football Playoff chances goodbye. Speaking of the CFP, this could be an important factor in Tech's inclusion this year. Texas Tech currently has the one-loss appeal that could get them into the field as an at-large bid, likely on the road to start the bracket. Losing the game would wipe that possibility out entirely. Something to consider is that Texas Tech just getting to the Big 12 title game probably wouldn't keep them safe in the CFP field regardless of the outcome in Arlington. With the 12-team CFP field expiring this year, the committee doesn't have much reason to protect the participants of conference championship games, which are fading away after this season to make way for the 24-team playoff next year. Texas Tech's J'Koby Williams runs with the ball against Arizona State during a Big 12 Conference football game, Saturday, Oct. 17, 2026, at Galaxy Stadium. The fired coach theory and TCU TCU made the move to part ways with Sonny Dykes following the team's 38-17 loss to Utah. Things haven't worked out well in Fort Worth since Dykes took the Horned Frogs to the national championship game. Despite two nine-win seasons since then, TCU has lacked consistency in a Big 12 that's been gettable with some form of success the last few years. The question for TCU becomes: will it follow the trend of firing your coach and coming out the next game with your hair on fire? TCU is the fifth power-conference team to have parted with its head coach during the 2026 season, the others being Baylor, NC State, Maryland, and Florida State. Of those four other teams switching coaches in season, three of them won their next game, two of them (Baylor and NC State) earning wins of 21 points or more. This theory doesn't always come to fruition, however. During the 2025 coaching cycle, six power-conference programs fired coaches during the season and just one of them won their next game following the axing. That one win came from Virginia Tech, which beat Wofford, so it barely counts. Score prediction for Texas Tech football vs TCU Texas Tech 34, TCU 31: TCU's staff and players are all trying to impress whoever the next head coach is, so they'll be pulling out all the stops in this one. Texas Tech has to manage that, but the home crowd gets them back to Arlington. away.headline: Backup QB likely to earn first start for TCU vs. No. 2 Utah after injury update
away.blurb: Senior quarterback Jaden Craig was initially expected to start and was listed as probable in the first Big 12 player availability report on Wednesday night. TCU head coach Sonny Dykes also said Tuesday that he believed Craig would be able to play. But Craig was downgraded to doubtful in Friday’s injury report and seems unlikely to play against the Utes. Craig was hobbled with an ankle injury during TCU’s 20-10 win over Kanas State last Saturday. Saturday night might mark the start of the Adam Schobel era for TCU football. The sophomore quarterback is expected to earn his first start when the Horned Frogs (5-5, 3-4) host No. 2 Utah (10-0, 7-0) at 8 p.m. Saturday at Amon G. Carter Stadium on Fox. “I would expect him to play, I think he was a lot better today than he was yesterday,” Dykes said Tuesday. “I would anticipate him being able to practice tomorrow and play on Saturday. That would be my guess.” Schobel has played sparingly this season, with just one passing attempt and 11 yards on four carries. But the former four-star recruit is largely viewed as the quarterback of the future for the program. Schobel got his most extensive action of his career in the win over the Wildcats, mostly on designed quarterback runs, but will now be tasked to lead the Horned Frogs against the highest-ranked opponent to play in the Carter since No. 2 Texas in 1970. Starting quarterback Jaden Craig landed on Friday night's Big 12 availability report as doubtful, putting sophomore backup Adam Schobel in line to make his first career start, per ESPN's Pete Thamel. TCU listed Craig as probable earlier in the week before downgrading him Friday night. Losing Craig deals a major blow to a 5-5 Horned Frogs offense chasing bowl eligibility against an undefeated 10-0 Utah squad. The Harvard transfer ranks third in the Big 12 with 266.4 passing yards per game, completing 223 of 344 throws for 2,664 yards, 13 touchdowns and seven interceptions while adding four rushing scores. The 6-foot-5 former four-star recruit from Columbus, Texas, has seen limited action across three appearances this season. He threw one incomplete pass against the Grambling Tigers in September and logged four carries for 11 yards, including three rushes for three yards against Kansas State. TCU's injury woes extend beyond the quarterback room. The Horned Frogs also ruled out running back G'Ivori Graham and linebacker Keylan Abrams for Saturday's contest in Fort Worth, though defensive tackles Markis Deal and Ansel Din-Mbuh alongside edge rusher Cheta Ofili remain probable. Meanwhile, Utah ruled out safety Marcus Wimberly and listed long snapper Logan Castor as questionable. Throwing a first-time starter against the Big 12's top team is no easy task, but Schobel gets his shot to shock college football under the Fort Worth lights. An injury to the new catalyst certainly caused fans to hold their breath, but this report is a sigh of relief. It might get there again soon, but for now, the rivalry is in a holding pattern. Florida is 20th in the latest College Football Playoff rankings after winning two straight to turn the season back around after a rough stretch. Florida State is waiting for new head coach Glenn Schumann to start, but the Georgia defensive coordinator is still a little busy for a bit at his current gig. Win this, and it'll be the program's first eight-win regular season since 2020, when the Gators played for the SEC title. Florida State has played well under interim head coach Rick Stockstill, but when it had a chance for a sixth win and bowl eligibility, it lost to NC State 28-10 last week. It gets one more shot. Florida has won five of the last seven in the series. How To Watch Florida vs Florida State Date: Friday, November 27, 2026 Game Time: 3:30 PM ET TV: ABC Location: Doak Campbell Stadium, Tallahassee, FL – Week 13 Schedule, Game Previews – CFP and Bowl Projections Why Florida Will Win Florida State has to run well to win. The passing game is dangerous, but the Noles don't win when they bomb away. They win when they get things going on the ground, going 4-1 when running for 175 yards or more. It's possible to run on the Gators, but Florida State isn't Georgia, or even Missouri, when it comes to being able to grind. And then there's the other side. Florida is 7-0 when running for more than 120 yards. Run well on the Noles, beat the Noles. Why Florida State Will Win Everyone wants to win a rivalry game like this, and of course Florida will bring the full focus, but this is existential for the Seminoles. It'll be iffy whether or not the program would want to accept a bowl invite, or be able to, considering the regime change, but this is for six wins. This is for a bowl game. Florida's defense isn't bad, but it doesn't come up with enough third down stops. Florida State has to control the positive momentum from the start. It doesn't need big plays, but with its tempo, it has to keep the Gators on their heels with a good offensive balance. Florida vs Florida State Prediction, Betting Lines This should be fun. There's a new energy around the Florida State program, the team will come up with a strong first quarter, and then the Gator offense will start to take over. picks.blurb: Florida vs. Florida State Final Score Predictions: Experts predict fierce rivalry with programs in different spots - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football CFP And Bowl Games Steelers release Aaron Rodgers NBA Cup roundup Latest CFP rankings MLB free agency updates Viral Ga. Tech couple Florida Gators HC Jon Sumrall and Florida State Seminoles interim head coach Rick Stockstill Matt Pendleton-Imagn Images, Eric Canha-Imagn Images Craig Smith, Justin Churchill, Rob Gregson, Ryan Roberts, Tyler Forness · AtoZ Sports Wed, November 25, 2026 at 9:13 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Florida Gators can finish the regular season on a high note with a win over bitter rival Florida State Seminoles. The Florida Gators and Florida State Seminoles have historically had one of the best rivalries over the last 35 years. The 1990s were as fierce as it gets with Steve Spurrier and Bobby Bowden facing off to likely play for a national championship in multiple seasons. Then, we got Urban Meyer vs. Bobby Bowden in the 2000s before Jimbo Fisher ran the show for a decade, and the Gators had a revolving door. Now, Florida has a new head coach in Jon Sumrall, and the Seminoles finally fired Mike Norvell, with Georgia Bulldogs defensive coordinator Glenn Schumann having already accepted the job. It's a new era in the bitter rivalry, but it's primed to take a sharp step forward. Here's how our experts predicted the game. Georgia (29%), Notre Dame (16%) and Texas (12%) have the best chances to win the college football national title, according to the A to Z Sports CFB Playoff Predictor (updated November 22, 2026). Florida 27, Florida State 17 This Seminoles team just isn't very good, and you can look at a multitude of factors to come to that conclusion. Having a head coach ready to go two weeks before early signing period is a good start, but that won't help on the field. The Gators have been playing very well defensively, and the offense, despite multiple issues, has found their way forward. There is still a lot of room to grow there, but it's going to be plenty good enough to win a rivalry game. – Tyler Forness , A to Z Florida Florida 34, Florida State 17 The Florida-Florida State matchup is one that has certainly lost plenty of its luster over the last several years nationally, but it carried plenty of weight still in the Sunshine State. It looked like the Noles were building some momentum after firing Mike Norvell, having won two straight on the road over Boston College and Pitt, but things came crashing down on Saturday in an ugly 28-10 loss to fellow lame duck NC State. Florida is playing this one on the road, which is a good thing, given their road vs home performances with a couple of exceptions. Jaden Baugh and Aaron Philo run wild and deliver a comfortable win for the Gators. – Craig Smith , A to Z Miami Florida 27, Florida State 16 The Gators have been a bit of a Jekyll and Hyde team throughout the season, showing flashes of what they can be while also struggling with consistency at times. That is somewhat expected with a first-year head coach trying to establish his program while turning over a roster and building an identity. There have been some growing pains, but I think Florida puts together one of its more complete performances in this rivalry matchup. Jadan Baugh will be the difference-maker offensively, putting together a big afternoon on the ground and giving the Gators the physical presence they need to control the game. Florida State will have some success early, but I have a hard time trusting the Seminoles to put together four consistent quarters. I expect this game to be competitive through halftime before Florida starts to take control after the break. The Gators' ability to run the football and dictate the tempo will become increasingly important as the game progresses, while Florida State struggles to find enough answers offensively. The Seminoles fade in the second half, and Florida does enough on both sides of the ball to pull away for a rivalry win. – Ryan Roberts , A to Z Notre Dame Florida 33, Florida State 20 This was once one of the best games of rivalry weekend, but in recent years, the two schools have been dealing with coaching changes and programs in flux. The Gators have outperformed many expectations in year one of the Summerall campaign, but the Seminoles finally pulled the plug on the Mike Norvell era. Even still, all bets tend to be off on rivalry weekend, and anything can happen. But not in this one. The Gators have too much firepower on offense, and the Seminoles are not an outfit that can handle the physicality and mentality that Sumrall has installed in his program. At least, not yet. Give me the Gators, comfortably. – Rob Gregson , A to Z Alabama Florida 24, Florida State 21 The Florida Gators' season is kind of hanging on by a thread after it started out really well, but they're still a much better team than FSU, and it's not particularly close. Still, this game could be a close one. We saw FSU push Miami to overtime, and their offense and the way they play could do the same here. But ultimately, I see Florida winning this game. – Justin Churchill , A to Z Oklahoma Final Prediction for Florida vs. Florida State To nobody's surprise, our experts are in favor of the Gators here. It isn't the Seminoles year, and they are likely to fall to the orange and blue. This article was originally published on A to Z Sports. The Florida State Seminoles will attempt to become bowl-eligible for the first time since 2023 and wrap up their ACC schedule with a .500 record when they host the NC State Wolfpack at Doak Campbell Stadium Saturday afternoon. Kickoff is scheduled for 3:30 p.m. and will be televised on the ACCN. FSU will celebrate its annual Homecoming and Seminole Heritage game and will wear turquoise jerseys and pants for the first time in program history. FSU is 3-0 in Heritage games and 63-12-1 all-time on Homecoming, with 12 consecutive victories. Throughout Native American communities, turquoise represents harmony, friendship and fellowship. The team found out it would wear the jerseys Sunday when defensive back Zae Thomas, a member of the Seminole Tribe of Florida, displayed the uniforms in the team meeting. For more information on FSU’s unique relationship with the Seminole Tribe of Florida and Seminole Heritage, visit noles.co/Heritage. Florida State football to wear new uniform combination against NC State to honor Seminole Heritage Florida State (5-5, 3-4 ACC) and NC State will meet for the 45th time, with the Noles leading the series, 27-17, including a 16-6 record in Doak. However, NC State has won the last four matchups with Florida State and six of the last seven meetings. Last year, the 11-21 loss at NC State likely cost the 5-win Seminoles the opportunity to become bowl eligible. Under interim head coach Rick Stockstill, the Seminoles will attempt to win their third consecutive game before closing out the season against the Florida Gators at home on Black Friday afternoon, again with another short week to prepare. The last time FSU won 3 straight games was to open the 2025 season before then losing 7 of the next 9 games. The Wolfpack (4-6, 2-5 ACC) also fired their head coach, Dave Doeren, midseason, ending his 14-year tenure as the winningest coach in Wolfpack history, compiling a 98-74 overall record, including 11 bowl appearances and 10 winning seasons. Former NFL quarterback and former Chuck Amato-coached NC State alum, Phillip Rivers, bringing six years’ experience as a Catholic high school football head coach, was officially hired as the new head coach for NC State earlier this week, effective next season. It has been reported that he will travel to Tallahassee along with the Wolfpack team. Rivers signed a reported five-year deal starting at $3.25 million in total compensation for his first year ($2.4375 million base salary plus $812,500 in supplemental income). This is roughly half of Doeren’s previous $6.375 million salary, making Rivers one of the lowest-paid Power 4 coaches. NC State’s interim head coach Todd Goebbel led the team to a 31–10 win over California before suffering a 41–3 blowout loss to Duke and a 34–31 collapse against Syracuse, where the Wolfpack blew an 11-point lead in the final five minutes. Junior 6’6” quarterback CJ Bailey Jr. has completed 186 of his 295 passes attempted for 2,289 yards with 14 TDs and 5 interceptions. Sophomore quarterback Will Wilson, who has only completed 9 of 12 passes for 35 yards, has scored 8 rushing touchdowns for the Wolfpack during his time behind center despite NC State starting seven different lineup combinations on the offensive line in their 10 games due to injuries. Sophomore running back Jayden “Duke” Scott leads the team in rushing with 504 yards on 81 attempts for a 6.22 yard/rush average, along with 5 touchdowns. On defense, linebacker Popo Aguirre leads the team in tackles with 85, followed by CB Brian Nelson II with 47. LB Elijah Satchell leads the team in sacks with five. In their last outing, FSU wrapped up their road schedule with arguably their best defensive performance of the season so far, a 16-10 win at Pittsburgh, under interim defensive coordinator Ernie Sims. FSU’s defense held Pitt, previously ranked 24th in total offense (446), to just 306 total yards, or 140 yards below their season average. The Noles defense allowed only 10 points to the Panthers, 22 points fewer than Pitt’s season average of 31.9 points/game, forced a crucial fourth-and-one turnover on downs in the third quarter, deflected six passes, recorded an interception, and sealed the game with a 4th-down stop on Pitt’s final drive. Florida State’s defense shines in road win over Pitt as Seminoles get back to .500 Florida State quarterback Ashton Daniels ranks in the top 20 nationally in six statistical categories: 5th Passing Yards Per Completion 14.61 9th Rushing Touchdowns 13 12th Points Responsible For 166 14th Total Touchdowns 13 15th Points Responsible For Per Game 16.6 16th Yards Per Pass Attempt 8.75 Additionally, Daniels ranks 22nd in the ESPN Total QBR with a 75.7 rating. Florida State vs NCST head-to-head stats comparison FSU kicker Gabe Panikowski is 26-for-26 on field goal attempts in his NCAA career, including 11-for-11 this season. He is the only active kicker (min. 15 attempts) in any NCAA division who is perfect in his career, and his 26 consecutive made field goals at the NCAA level is the longest active streak. Panikowski accounted for 23 points in the two road wins. He became the first FBS player since 2023 with a touchdown, field goal, and 4+ extra points in the win at BC before kicking a season-high three field goals at Pitt. His 47-yarder against Pitt was a season-long. FSU TE Corbyn Fordham is the younger brother of NC State linebacker Caden Fordham, who played against FSU in 2025 and recorded 15 tackles for NC State. NC State was the first team to defeat Florida State at Doak after the Seminoles joined the ACC in 1992. 2026 FSU Schedule Preview: NC State Wolfpack-A real toss-up on paper Florida State is currently trending as a 10.5-point favorite with the over/under set at 56.5 points, according to FanDuel. NoleThruandThru (season record: 8-2) FSU may be down 12 running backs but with Ernie Sims’ stare boring holes through opponent foreheads, not even Philip Rivers can save the Pack this time. Give me that sixth win, Stock!!! FSU 23, NC State 17 Tony Morris (season record: 5-0) Homecoming game, beautiful jerseys, gorgeous field. A chance to see Coach Stockstill win a game at home as interim head coach. Gimme the boys in turquoise! FSU 24, NC State 1 4 Seminole Uprising (season record: 7-3) I wish I had time to change my pick from last week after hearing about Pitt’s quarterback change. Oh well. Turning our attention to Saturday, it is hard not to see the Seminoles as a bit of a vibes pick right now. Even though Florida State faced the Panthers’ third-string QB, a road win after a short week will do wonders for this team’s confidence. Meanwhile, NCSU blew another game in ridiculous fashion and is more focused on their new head coach than on the result of this weekend’s game. Injuries are my main concern, but Vegas doesn’t think so, listing the Noles as a 10.5-point favorite. While I do not see a double-digit victory, I do believe FSU becomes bowl-eligible Saturday. Normally this game would scare me, but for two reasons. It’s at home, and unlike Pitt, NC State’s defense is terrible, ranking 109th in the country per FEI, while FSU’s offense is holding steady at 19th. The other side of the ball is a more even matchup, so I think whether FSU wins or loses comes down to the Seminole offense and QB Ashton Daniels. Despite all of FSU’s injuries on offense, which have admittedly shrunk their ceiling, I think they’ll find enough explosive plays to put up enough points to become bowl-eligible. NC State’s defense is pitiful, and Florida State’s offense is pretty good. Meanwhile, FSU’s defense is far below average, and NC State’s offense is bad. I think for this reason, FSU gets the win in another close game, and they FINALLY get back to a bowl game. Sad, because I’m rather fond of CJ Bailey. FSU 24, NC State 21 Curt Weiler (season record: 7-3, ATS: 3-7) If Florida State wants to get bowl eligible, I would advise it does so this week. Florida is beatable but also capable of delivering a much better result than this NC State team. Thankfully for the Seminoles, I think they get it done somewhat comfortably. The Wolfpack have been leaking some serious oil, losing their last two games and four of their last five. And it’s not to feel like the Seminoles enter this one 2-0 in the Rick Stockstill era. FSU 34, NC State 24 LastNoleOfKrypton (season record: 6-2) On Monday Ernie Sims said ‘we’re going to test his will’ in regard to NC State QB CJ Bailey. FSU will be down its best edge rusher Rylan Kennedy so expect a lot of heavy pressure and different looks. Bailey has been known to turn it over under consistent pressure so FSU should be able to score off some shorter fields. FSU goes bowling for the first time since 2023. FSU 34, NC State 21 Matt Minnick (season record: 7-3; ATS: 6-4) Playing in Doak for the first time under Coach Stockstill, FSU is looking to make it three in a row in ACC play for the first time since 2023. If the ‘Noles were even decently healthy I’d pick them in a runaway. NC State has given up 30+ points on 7 different occasions this season, including 41 to Duke and 34 to Syracuse in their last two games. However, FSU isn’t remotely healthy and the losses on offense have been particularly severe. Where does Stockstill turn if another running back is hurt? Can Ernie Sims’ defense step up big in back to back weeks? How will the turquoise endzones look after a few days of rain? It isn’t pretty, but the Seminoles get it done, reaching bowl eligibility with one game to go. FSU 27, NC State 23 Frank DNole (season record: 5-5) I expect FSU’s offense to score against NC State’s mid-average defense more often than not, that is, if they run Daniels to make up for the lack of running backs, even if he is banged up. That will open up the pass against NC State’s weak secondary. With news that Rylan Kennedy is now officially out, the defense’s job just got a little harder, not gonna lie. QB Bailey is predominantly a pocket passer and hasn’t been a run threat (74 attempts for 228 yards, 3.1 per carry, 22.8 yards per game, 3 TDs, long rush of 28 yards) this season. I think Ernie brings pressure more than he has. Their 6 losses have been to Virginia (5-5), Vanderbilt (4-6), Wake Forest (9-1), Stanford (5-5), Duke (7-3), and Syracuse (5-5). home.blurb: Florida hasn't lost to FSU since its horrific 5-7 season in 2023 when the Seminoles were a perfect 13-0 but still missed out on the College Football Playoffs. How Brown's Season-Ending Injury Impacts Florida vs. Florida State - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF How Brown's Season-Ending Injury Impacts Florida vs. Florida State (IMAGN Images via Reuters Connect) Jordon Lawrenz · Roundtable Sports Wed, November 25, 2026 at 12:00 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads As of Tuesday, Nov. 24, the Florida Gators officially shut down wide receiver Vernell Brown III for the rest of the season. This is news that came as no surprise , and it's crazy to see it take as long as it did. Brown had only suited up for four games this season, but he continued to appear on injury reports leading up to Florida's 34-27 win against Vanderbilt. The 7-4 Gators certainly could've used Brown in that brutal one-win stretch from Oct. 3 to Nov. 7, but at the end of the day they bounced back terrifically from Nov. 14 onward. Brown was a crucial part of this team's 4-0 start as he recorded 17 receptions for 271 yards with a pair of touchdowns. For reference, he's still third on the team in receiving yards, proving just how valuable he was during the few games when he was around. For the Gators, it's business as usual going into the final game of the year, a rivalry showdown at Florida State. Finally, Florida's offense knows it can move on once and for all without Brown. That's not a sentence they wanted to hear back on Sept. 26, but it's been a long time coming as his status had been in doubt for the better part of two months. Brown is only a sophomore, so the Gators risking further injury by putting him back on the field was never going to be the right answer. The Florida native made an immediate impact as a freshman with his 40 receptions for 512 yards. Obviously, this season took quite a turn with those losses to Missouri and South Carolina, and it doesn't feel like a coincidence that the offense scored fewer than 20 points in those games without Brown. Running back Jadan Baugh was not a factor in either of those games either, so that also didn't help the Gators chances when they lost their offensive superstar. When Brown and Baugh were both on the field, this team looked absolutely unstoppable. Now, it'll once again be up to Aaron Philo to keep this run-game going, though he looked much better through the air against the Commodores. Florida State enters this non-conference game at 5-6 overall, fighting for bowl eligibility against a Brown-less Gators offense.

The Badgers enter the rivalry matchup coming off their most convincing win of the season, a 42-10 blowout of Purdue. Colton Joseph led the way with 187 rushing yards and two touchdowns, while Darrion Dupree added another 125 yards and two scores. Minnesota has had an inconsistent season but remains a dangerous rivalry opponent . The Golden Gophers enter at 6-5 overall and 4-4 in Big Ten play, and they'll be motivated to keep the Axe after defeating Wisconsin 17-7 last season. Minnesota's defense presents a tougher challenge than Purdue, but the Badgers have shown what their offense can look like when Joseph and the rushing attack are clicking. Playing at Camp Randall should give Wisconsin another advantage. One would expect a competitive rivalry game, but the Badgers seem have enough momentum to finish the regular season with a statement win. 122nd time since 1897, Michigan and Ohio State will meet in a rivalry known as "The Game." Photo By - Reuters Connect. Charles Woodson (2) and Archie Griffin (45) are two key figures in the Michigan vs. Ohio State rivalry. Arguably the greatest rivalry in all of sports returns in Week 13 of the college football season, with Ohio State hosting Michigan at Ohio Stadium in Columbus, Ohio, at noon ET (FOX) on Saturday, Nov. 28. This year's edition of the Michigan vs. Ohio State rivalry , known simply as The Game, is different from recent years, with both programs enduring down seasons and neither contending for a national championship. Some would argue that makes this the purest version of the rivalry, with both teams fueled by their dislike for each other and little else. Ohio State is a 10.5-point favorite, and my college football picks back the Buckeyes to win big. Michigan vs Ohio State rivalry history: The Game Wins (official; six ties) 9 (1901-1909) Longest win streak 8 (2012-2019) Largest margin of victory 1027-367-36 (.731) Program record 997-342-53 (.735) Claimed national titles (recognized) Conference championships Heisman winners Consensus All-Americans Weeks in the AP Poll Weeks at No. 1 Bowl games (record) NFL draft picks First-round picks Few rivalries feature two teams as successful as Michigan and Ohio State . That history makes their mutual hatred even more intense. The Wolverines and the Buckeyes have both won plenty of national championships, produced multiple Heisman Trophy winners, and sent countless players to the NFL, but more than anything else, they take pride in beating each other. This rivalry is built as much on program success as it is on animosity. Michigan has more wins than any other program in college football history, and Ohio State has a higher winning percentage than any other program in college football history. The Game often has major implications for the national championship and the Heisman Trophy race. It all began in 1897, and The Game has been played every season since 1918, except in 2020 due to the COVID-19 pandemic. Its history stretches from Fielding Yost's early dominance through Woody Hayes and Bo Schembechler's Ten-Year War, Jim Tressel and Urban Meyer's successful runs, and Jim Harbaugh's revival of Michigan. This is the college football rivalry. Recent Michigan-Ohio State results Nov. 29, 2025 27-9 (Ohio State) Ohio State (-9.5) Nov. 30, 2024 13-10 (Michigan) Michigan (+19.5) Nov. 25, 2023 30-24 (Michigan) Michigan (-3.5) Nov. 26, 2022 45-23 (Michigan) Michigan (+8.5) Nov. 27, 2021 42-27 (Michigan) Michigan (+7) Nov. 30, 2019 56-27 (Ohio State) Ohio State (-9) Nov. 24, 2018 62-39 (Ohio State) Ohio State (+3.5) Nov. 25, 2017 31-20 (Ohio State) Michigan (+12.5) Nov. 26, 2016 30-27 (Ohio State) Michigan (+4.5) Nov. 28, 2015 42-13 (Ohio State) Ohio State (-1.5) History of the Michigan vs Ohio State rivalry When did the Michigan vs Ohio State rivalry start? The Michigan vs. Ohio State rivalry began in 1897 and was immediately a natural rivalry because of the bordering states' history with the Toledo War (a boundary dispute between the states over the Toledo Strip). The Wolverines won the first matchup on Oct. 16, 1897, in Ann Arbor, 34-0. The programs didn't meet again until a 0-0 tie in 1900, then played every season through 1912. Michigan went 12-0-2 against Ohio State from 1897 to 1912. The Buckeyes didn't win The Game for the first time until 1919, beating Michigan 13-3 to spark a three-game winning streak. However, Michigan owned the rivalry, for the most part, until Hayes arrived in 1951. The Wolverines went 32-12-4 against Ohio State from 1897 to 1950. Why is it called The Game? Michigan vs. Ohio State is known to most as The Game because of its importance to both fan bases and college football nationally. The matchup has closed out the regular season since 1935, and usually there's plenty on the line when these teams meet. Before Big Ten expansion, the winner of The Game would frequently win the conference and head to the Rose Bowl for a chance at a national title. And in later years, The Game would play a key role in setting the Big Ten Championship Game matchup. The loser of The Game generally considers the season a disappointment. What was the Ten-Year War? What kicked off the Ten-Year War between Michigan and Ohio State was the Wolverines hiring Hayes' protege, Schembechler, in 1969. Schembechler had been an assistant under Hayes at Ohio State from 1958 to 1962 before following in Hayes' footsteps and becoming head coach at Miami (OH). Both Hayes (1949-1950) and Schembechler (1963-1968) coached at Miami (Ohio) before taking over Ohio State and Michigan. Hayes went 12-6 against Michigan in The Game from 1951-1968 and flipped the once maize and blue-dominated rivalry to the scarlet and grey. That led Michigan in a new direction with the hiring of Schembechler, who immediately made his presence felt. In Schembechler's first game against Ohio State, Michigan pulled off "the upset of the century" by beating the No. 1 Buckeyes 24-12 and ending their 22-game winning streak. That victory marked the beginning of the Ten-Year War. From 1970 to 1975, in four of the six meetings, both Ohio State and Michigan were ranked in the top five. During the Ten-Year War, the programs shared the Big Ten title multiple times, with Michigan ultimately having the upper hand, going 5-4-1 against Ohio State. The war ended after the 1978 season, when Hayes was fired for punching Clemson linebacker Charlie Bauman after an interception in the Gator Bowl. It was during the Ten-Year War that Ohio State began its tradition of referring to Michigan as "That Team Up North" when Hayes referred to the Wolverines as such. Best moments in the Michigan vs Ohio State rivalry The Snow Bowl (1950) Among the most famous games in the Michigan vs. Ohio State rivalry, the Snow Bowl was exactly what it sounds like: a game in a blizzard. The blizzard was so bad that the Buckeyes were given the option to cancel the game (they would have won the Big Ten title by default if they had), but Ohio State wanted to play its rival. All in all, the teams combined to punt the ball 45 times, with many of the punts coming on first down as they battled for field position and hoped the other team would fumble. Michigan would block two punts, one resulting in a safety and the other a touchdown, to win 9-3. The Wolverines didn't complete a single pass or gain a single first down, but took home the Big Ten title with the win. Ohio State head coach Wes Fesler would resign after the loss, leading to Hayes being hired. The Upset of the Century (1969) In Schembechler's first game against his former boss, Michigan would upset undefeated No. 1-ranked Ohio State 24-12. The Buckeyes were riding a 22-game winning streak and gunning for their second straight national title, but an all-time performance from Barry Pierson (three interceptions and a 60-yard punt return that set up a touchdown) would end Ohio State's shot at a championship. Here are our predictions for the game: Ohio State vs. Michigan predictions Joey Kaufman, Columbus Dispatch: Michigan 24, Ohio State 20 : It's felt like fool's gold in recent weeks to pick Ohio State to end its late-season slide, so there's hesitation to pull that lever. Michigan's offensive futility should make it easy to go chalk with the Buckeyes . It averages the second-fewest points per game among Power 4 teams and has vacillated between starting Bryce Underwood and Tommy Carr at quarterback. But the Wolverines don't need to score much with a suffocating defense. They also have a bit of momentum after an upset of unbeaten UCLA last weekend. The vibes just seem better in Ann Arbor, which might matter the most with only bragging right at stake. Rob Oller, Columbus Dispatch: Ohio State 17, Michigan 16 : I went back and forth on this one before deciding that Michigan's offense is simply too anemic to pull off a win in Ohio Stadium. The Wolverines rank 130th in first downs, 128th in passing yards and 99th in rushing yardage per game. On the flip side, UM's defense, ranked ninth nationally, is the most reliable piece on either team, so if the Wolverines can hold OSU to 14 points they have a great chance at winning in Columbus for a third straight time. It likely comes down to which team's head and heart are into a game where the only thing on the line is bragging rights. Brianna Mac Kay, Columbus Dispatch: Ohio State 21, Michigan 17 : Ohio State's offense with Luke Fahey at quarterback has shown flashes of promise, primarily before the defense put the Buckeyes in a deficit across the past four games. If the defense can keep Michigan under its season average of 18.3 points per game, which ranks 129th in the country, the offense should be able to put together enough momentum to finish the season with a win over the Wolverines. Dan Aulbach, Columbus Dispatch: Ohio State 17, Michigan 13 : We finally get to see what happens when a stoppable force meets a moveable object. On the one hand, Michigan has the same starting quarterback as last year's edition of the rivalry, but Bryce Underwood has severely underperformed his expectations. Michigan's offense is lethargic, but Ohio State's defense has allowed 30-plus points in three of its last four games. Michigan's defense is elite (ninth in scoring defense), but so is Jeremiah Smith . The Buckeyes proved earlier in the year they can play and win against a defense-first team in Iowa, so I'll reluctantly pick the Buckeyes. picks.blurb: Urban Meyer Makes Ohio State-Michigan Prediction That Buckeyes Fans Won’t Like - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football CFP And Bowl Games Steelers release Aaron Rodgers NBA Cup roundup Latest CFP rankings MLB free agency updates Viral Ga. Tech couple Urban Meyer Makes Ohio State-Michigan Prediction That Buckeyes Fans Won’t Like Former Ohio State head coach Urban Meyer is concerned about the Buckeyes heading into their game against Michigan Getty Michael Gallagher · HEAVY Mon, November 23, 2026 at 8:25 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads ANN ARBOR, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 29: Bryce Underwood #19 of the Michigan Wolverines is pursued by Kenyatta Jackson Jr. #97 of the Ohio State Buckeyes during the fourth quarter at Michigan Stadium on November 29, 2025 in Ann Arbor, Michigan. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) Getty Ohio State head coach Ryan Day is sticking with QB Luke Fahey after losing his last two games Getty It's been a rough month for the Ohio State Buckeyes. Ohio State started 6-1 but has lost three of its last four games. The latest was Saturday's 31-28 loss at Nebraska, which officially knocked the Buckeyes out of the College Football Playoff race. All that's left now is "The Game" against the Michigan Wolverines on Saturday in Columbus. On paper, Ohio State has the better roster. Even former Buckeyes head coach Urban Meyer admits that. Meyer, who went 7-0 against Michigan during his time in Columbus, still picked Ohio State to win. However, it sounds like he wouldn't be all that surprised if Michigan ended up leaving Columbus with a win. Urban Meyer's 1 Major Michigan Concern GettyMichigan and Ohio State both head into the Big Game with serious question marks Meyer spoke on stage at an event in a video posted Sunday by 10TV Sports' Adam King, and he didn't sugarcoat where Ohio State stands. "The roster's better — Ohio State — but the best unit performing right now is the Wolverine defense. And that concerns me a little bit," Meyer said . "They really hammered UCLA. You got to think, the other side of the ball for the Wolverines is terrible — they're last in the country. And so, to still have decent numbers — only one team has over 21 points on them all year, and that was Oregon — that's a legit defense. "On offense, we got the best player in the country, maybe the best player to ever play college football — that's how good Jeremiah is. But we also have a backup quarterback, and the offensive line is not playing great. So, I think this is going to be a rock fight; a low-scoring game, and I think whoever punches the hardest is going to win the game. I expect it to be a 17-10, 17-14 game and I got the Buckeyes." The numbers back up Meyer's remarks. Michigan ranks 17th nationally in scoring defense (17.5 points per game) and ninth in total defense (278.3 yards per game). And Oregon, which beat Michigan 31-7, is the only team to score more than 21 points on the Wolverines all season. The Wolverines' defense was at its best last Saturday in an 18-16 triple-overtime upset of previously unbeaten No. 4 UCLA. Michigan held the Bruins to 187 yards through three quarters and finished with three forced turnovers and four sacks. Why Urban Meyer Expects a Rock Fight vs. Michigan GettyOhio State head coach Ryan Day is sticking with QB Luke Fahey The biggest reason for Meyer's worry is at quarterback. Starter Julian Sayin hurt his right (throwing) arm in Ohio State's 19-15 win over Indiana on Oct. 17, and he isn't expected back for Michigan. That leaves true freshman Luke Fahey under center. Fahey went 16 of 27 for 259 yards, two touchdowns, and an interception at Nebraska. But nearly all of that came early: He was 9 of 12 for 163 yards and two scores in the first half, then 7 of 15 for 96 yards after halftime. Jeremiah Smith did his part (six catches, 165 yards, two touchdowns), tying Terry Glenn's Ohio State single-season record with 17 receiving TDs. Meyer also didn't pull any punches when it came to the other side of the ball for Michigan. "That defense is legit, legit because that offense is pathetic up there. It's the worst offense in college football, yet they're in almost all the games," Meyer said . "Their defense, what they did to UCLA, was absolutely phenomenal. Our defense has been up-and-down a little bit, but their offense stinks. I see this being a very low-scoring game. This is Ohio State-Wolverine football. The toughest team is going to win this game." Michigan's offense isn't quite the worst in the country, but it's close. The Wolverines rank 131st nationally in scoring (18.3 points per game). It's quite a shift for Meyer, who reportedly called the 2026 Wolverines a "train wreck" in early October. The Buckeyes (7-4) and Wolverines (6-5) kick off at noon ET Saturday at Ohio Stadium on Fox. Ohio State dropped another game last week to the Nebraska Cornhuskers, seeing its record fall down to 7-4 on the season. The Buckeyes dream of getting into the College Football Playoff is now over, and the team can look ahead to next year. But there is still a massive game on the schedule this week, with the Buckeyes hosting the rival Michigan Wolverines. While both teams have struggled this season, this is the biggest rivalry in college football, with each side understanding that bragging rights are on the line. No matter what the records are, or how each team is playing, this game tends to have fireworks involved with it . The Buckeyes could look to salvage their season a little bit if they can take the home win over Michigan. If anything, the Buckeyes can sell potential prospects and fans on a win over Michigan, which is one of the larger parts of the season. Ohio State's season may have not gone to plan, but this is a game that they can't lose. Ohio State has gone 5-3 in Big Ten games this season, with the program being in unfamiliar territory at this point. The Buckeyes can make it up by taking down Michigan this week, giving their fans something before the year ends. As for Michigan, they will enter the game with a record of 6-5 for the year, coming off a big win over the UCLA Bruins. The Wolverines have gone 3-5 in Big Ten play, and the Buckeyes want to add to the loss column. Entering the game, the Buckeyes are being viewed as heavy favorites, despite how the year has gone for the team. According to the ESPN matchup predictor , Ohio State has been given an 89.1 percent chance of winning this game over Michigan. One of the biggest parts to the game for the Buckeyes is to protect quarterback Luke Fahey, especially against this tough Michigan defense. Fahey hasn't done well as the team's starter after replacing Julian Sayin due to injury, but this could be his chance to make a statement. If the team can protect Fahey in the game, it would at least give the Buckeyes a better chance to win the rivalry matchup. Ohio State has the tools to win this game, but the coaching staff is going to have to keep guys focused the rest of the week.

Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Debate it all you want, but Michigan vs Ohio State, in football, is the best rivalry in all of American sports. Alabama vs Auburn is as nasty as it gets, but that's a high-end, in-state war. Yankees vs Red Sox and Bears vs Packers – those get played several times a year. Duke vs North Carolina in basketball gets played at least twice. With Michigan and Ohio State, you have two behemoth universities from two different states, and it all comes down to this one game that, when it's at its biggest and best, stops the sports world cold. This isn't at its biggest and best this year, which means it's all about the rivalry. Trust me, you can be Michigan or Ohio State and win the national title, but if you don't beat the other, the season has a hole in it. As bad as the season has been for the Wolverines or Buckeyes, someone's year will be made. Michigan finally got bowl-eligible with its thrilling win over UCLA last week. Ohio State won 27-9 last year to break a run of four straight Michigan wins. The Buckeyes haven't beaten the Wolverines in Columbus since 2018. How To Watch Michigan vs Ohio State Date: Saturday, November 28, 2026 Game Time: 12:00 PM ET TV: FOX Location: Ohio Stadium, Columbus, OH – Week 13 Schedule, Game Previews – CFP and Bowl Projections Why Michigan Will Win The defense continues to be a force. It's ninth in the nation overall, with a nasty run defense that held up well against both UCLA's pounding style last week and Oregon's flash and speed before that. Rutgers is the only team to average more than four yards per carry against this Wolverine bunch. Ohio State's running game isn't good enough to carry the team. This is about as simple as it gets for a Wolverine team without a steady passing game. Run the ball well, force field goals, repeat. The Michigan ground attack hasn't been too bad, and in this, it just has to keep the clock moving – having Bryce Underwood under center should help. Ohio State is 1-4 when allowing over 85 rushing yards. Michigan is 6-2 when running for more than 80. But … Why Ohio State Will Win The Michigan passing attack is just plain putrid. It actually worked against Iowa, of all teams, but it's wildly inconsistent and doesn't do a thing downfield. Ohio State has to get up fast. It was able to do it in the 41-28 loss to Oregon, and scored first last week against Nebraska. Positive momentum will be everything to this Buckeye bunch. It won't have a problem if Michigan tries to keep running, but it does have to keep Underwood from finding a passing groove. The Buckeyes are now 0-4 against teams that connect on more than 60% of their passes. Underwood is hitting just 55% of his throws on the year. The star caught three passes for 40 yards and a key score in last year's Buckeye win, and made five grabs for 35 yards and a touchdown in 2024. Ohio State quarterback Luke Fahey will have another nice game – he hasn't been the problem in this rough run over the last month. He'll hit one deep shot to Smith, and that will be about enough. The Buckeye offense won't be anything pretty, but it'll get just enough points off a few scoring drives to hold up. Ohio State's defense will finally have a solid game again, but that's more because Michigan's offense just won't move. It's Michigan vs Ohio State. Forget everything else – it just means more. Wolverines Football Updated: Nov. 24, 2026, 9:28 a.m. | Published: Nov. 23, 2026, 11:55 a.m. Aaron McMann | amcmann@mlive.com ANN ARBOR, Mich. — Kyle Whittingham said Monday morning that Michigan football would be sticking with Bryce Underwood at quarterback this week. Given what happened over the weekend, the Wolverines’ upset win over No. 4 UCLA, 18-16, in overtime, it makes sense. The sophomore didn’t put up impressive numbers, but did enough to help the team -- and completed the game-winning two-point conversion throw. “Bryce is the guy,” Whittingham told reporters ahead of Saturday’s rivalry showdown at Ohio State (12 p.m., FOX). “Bryce is the guy and Tommy (Carr) is the No. 2.” Whittingham did add a stipulator, calling it the plan “barring any(thing) unforeseen” like “getting dinged up in practice or something like that. “That’s how it will be,” Whittingham continued. away.headline: Report: Michigan QB Bryce Underwood dealing with injury heading into Ohio State game
away.blurb: At his press conference on Monday morning, Michigan head football coach Kyle Whittingham said that sophomore Bryce Underwood is set to start in The Game this weekend against Ohio State. However, we’ll see if he’s able to even play at all. Per 247Sports’ Matt Zenitz, Underwood is dealing with a lower-body injury that he suffered during Saturday’s stunning upset win over UCLA. His status is “in question” heading into The Game in Columbus this weekend. Underwood has had quite the roller coaster season. He started the first six games of the season before freshman Tommy Carr took over after halftime of the Penn State game. Carr was then benched two weeks ago during the game at Oregon, and Underwood has taken every snap since. Despite the injury, Whittingham told the media on Monday morning that Underwood is “the guy” at quarterback, and that “barring anything unforeseen, getting dinged up in practice or something like that,” he will start against the Buckeyes on Saturday. Underwood completed just 11-of-24 passes for 127 yards and one touchdown on Saturday vs UCLA. He also ran 13 times for five yards, losing one fumble in the process. On the season, he has completed 85-of-156 passes (54.5 percent) for 1,077 yards, six touchdowns and six interceptions, while also running 76 times for 230 yards and an additional two scores. Should Underwood not be able to play in this one, Carr will be the next man up for the Wolverines. The true freshman has completed 67-of-106 passes this season for 686 yards, two touchdowns and three interceptions. He’s also ran 49 times for 138 yards and three touchdowns. Michigan vs Ohio State is set for a noon kickoff on FOX.

home.headline: Ohio State's College Football Playoff dreams go up in smoke following loss to Nebraska
home.blurb: The Ohio State Buckeyes have one of the most expensive rosters in college football , but on Saturday, that didn't matter a lick. Nebraska rode a little home cooking and some fourth quarter magic to secure one of its biggest wins in the last decade, taking down the Buckeyes 31-28. Despite the heroics of wide receiver Jeremiah Smith, who hauled in six catches for 165 yards and two scores, Ohio State was not able to overcome the loss of quarterback Julian Sayin, losing for the third time in four games since his injury. Though it could be argued the Buckeye offense did enough to grab the W, since the Cornhuskers controlled the game to the tune of 31 points and 176 yards rushing. Despite the relatively identical numbers in the yardage department, the Huskers ran nearly twice as many plays as the Buckeyes and had the ball for almost a full quarter longer. Couple that with relatively mistake-free football (Nebraska was plus-two in the turnover battle), and you get what is perhaps head coach Matt Rhule 's signature win in his fourth year in Lincoln. If the Huskers can win next week in Iowa City, they will have completed the most successful season since Mike Riley won nine games in 2016. For the Buckeyes, this almost certainly drives the final nail in the coffin for their CFP chances , and punctuates a season that started with so much promise before falling off the rails. The Buckeyes were 6-1 heading into their Halloween showdown with USC, but the aforementioned injury to Sayin proved to be too much to overcome. Ohio State can salvage what's left of their season by defeating bitter rival Michigan in next week's edition of "The Game" in Columbus. The Maize and Blue haven't exactly been a free win for the Buckeyes since the turn of the decade, though, as the Wolverines are 4-1 in the rivalry post-COVID. Regardless, it's sure to be a long, cold offseason in central Ohio, while a Nebraska program in purgatory has suddenly found new life. home.blurb: Norton has missed the last two games as well, as he continues to deal with an undisclosed injury. It seems like he’s more likely to play against Ohio State than Frazier because Norton “would have been available in case of an emergency situation last week.” Whittingham went on to say he hopes Norton will be able to return this week, but it’s too early in the week to tell. Marshall was sidelined for the UCLA game after having just five carries in the loss to Oregon the week before. Whittingham previously said Marshall’s inconsistent workload wasn’t “injury related” but he was out with an injury last week, so his status at Ohio State remains unclear. “We’re hoping that we get him back this week,” Whittingham told the media on Monday. JJ Buchanan, Andrew Sprague (out) Buchanan and Sprague were both officially ruled out for the remainder of the season by Whittingham a week ago. After going down with a shoulder injury in the loss to Oregon, Buchanan’s first season at Michigan came to an end prematurely. Meanwhile, Sprague has been out since mid-September with an undisclosed injury and is out for the year. The Michigan Wolverines face the Ohio State Buckeyes in college football’s most intense rivalry on Saturday in Columbus. Heading into the latest edition of The Game, Michigan had several players on the Big Ten’s midweek availability report. Underwood is reportedly “dealing with a lower-body injury” and “his status is in question” at Ohio State. The sophomore quarterback regained the starting job last week and will start against the Buckeyes if he’s healthy. However, the severity of his injury remains a mystery, as Underwood hopes to lead Michigan again this week. Frazier was expected to miss the rest of the year after suffering an injury against Michigan State and missing the last two games. However, it appears Frazier could suit up at Ohio State. It’s difficult to know how likely it is he returns this weekend, but head coach Kyle Whittingham said earlier this week that “he’s making progress” and “we’re waiting on a thumbs up or down.”

Tech couple Story by Wildcats Wire Louisville defense preview: Kentucky has to finish drives Braxton Howard, UK Wildcats Wire · Wildcats Wire Wed, November 25, 2026 at 11:27 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Kentucky football is in a must win scenario heading into the Governor's Cup against Louisville to avoid a winless November. Over this losing streak, the Wildcats offense has been the main issue, in my opinion. They have scored just 34 points over the last three weeks, they are averaging just 11 points per game. We previewed the explosive Louisville offense, so Kentucky will have to match them to win this football game. Louisville ranks 41st in the FBS, allowing 128 rushing yards per game. They have allowed 12 rushing touchdowns on the season and teams have averaged 3.5 yards per carry against them. Kentucky will likely be without starting running back CJ Baxter, who was injured against Missouri. This puts a ton of pressure on Jovantae Barnes and Jason Patterson to carry the workload in this game, and the Kentucky offensive line has to dominate the line of scrimmage to open up holes for them on the ground. The Cardinals run defense is the strength of their defense, but they are one of the worst teams in the FBS defending the passing game. Louisville ranks 121st in the FBS in pass defense, as they allow 243 passing yards per game. They are similar to Kentucky in the sense they live off creating turnovers, the Cardinals have 12 interceptions this season. Kentucky will have plenty of opportunities in the passing game, as the Cardinals are the worst pass defense the Wildcats have faced all season, statistically. I would expect another huge game from Kenny Darby and Willie Rodriguez, who have been the clear top two targets for the Cats all season. Louisville will struggle to find answers for those two players in this game, but it will come down to the rest of the group making plays. We need to see DJ Miller get more involved, he has been inconsistent this season but we have seen flashes. Kentucky needs another pass catcher to emerge so it is not all on the shoulders of Darby and Rodriguez. Kentucky will be able to move the football, but they have to finish drives. This led to a loss against Missouri, as the Wildcats only scored 14 points and one touchdown on the Tigers despite having seven trips to the red zone. This game will play out similar to the one we just watched if Kentucky fails to finish drives. Louisville is similar to Missouri, they have a big play offense that can create scoring opportunities regardless of where they are on the field. The biggest difference is the defenses, that is a great Missouri defense that Kentucky had success on last week. It should be a lot easier for the Wildcats to finish drives and capitalize on their scoring opportunities in this game. All eyes are on this Kentucky offense showing signs of life after a three game losing streak where they have struggled in multiple areas. Will Stein gets to face the team he played for in his first ever Governor's Cup as a head coach, and his offense finding success will be the key to the Wildcats bringing the trophy back to Lexington. After a great start to the season, with a 7-1 record heading into the bye week and November, Kentucky Football has now lost three straight games. The Wildcats have suffered losses to Tennessee on the road, Florida at home, and most recently Missouri on the road. Heading into the Missouri matchup, Kentucky was ranked No. 16 in the AP Top 25 Poll. However, after a 28-14 loss to the Tigers, the Wildcats have officially fallen out of the rankings. Many Kentucky fans expected the team to bounce back against Florida at home, especially with a sellout crowd at Kroger Field. Unfortunately, the Wildcats came up short on their final drive. Meanwhile, against Missouri, Kentucky had several opportunities to score more than 14 points but struggled to capitalize in the red zone. Sacks, turnovers, and turnovers on downs ultimately prevented the Wildcats from putting more points on the board. While the final three games of the season have not gone well, not many fans expected Kentucky to reach seven wins during Will Stein’s first year, especially considering the difficult schedule the Wildcats faced. Although some fans are disappointed with how the past few weeks have unfolded, many are still pleased with what Stein has accomplished during his first season. Stein has even described the year as successful, despite the possibility of losing to Louisville at home to close out the regular season. Hopefully, that will not be the case. Now, let’s get into the Louisville matchup, as they face off for the Governor’s Cup. Louisville Cardinals (8-3) Kentucky holds the all-time series lead against Louisville, 20-17, but the Wildcats have lost their last two matchups against the Cardinals. Last year, Louisville went on to win 41-0, shutting out Kentucky on the road. That result ultimately contributed to former head coach Mark Stoops being fired. In 2024, the Cardinals also defeated the Wildcats, winning 41-14 at Kroger Field in another disappointing performance for Kentucky. Before that, Kentucky won five straight games against Louisville. Now, Will Stein, who played at Louisville, is leading the Wildcats and will face his former team for the first time as Kentucky’s head coach. As for Louisville, the Cardinals got off to a rocky start, opening the season with a 2-3 record. However, they have since won six consecutive games and improved to 8-3 on the year. A major reason for Louisville’s early struggles was its defense, which had difficulty stopping opposing offenses. Meanwhile, the Cardinals’ offense continued to put up plenty of points, keeping them competitive in several games. Now, things have started to come together for head coach Jeff Brohm and his team. Louisville will look to win its third consecutive game against Kentucky and improve to 9-3 on the season. The Wildcats will certainly have their hands full, as Louisville averages 38.6 points per game, which ranks eighth in the country. The Cardinals also allow 23.4 points per game, ranking 55th nationally. Kentucky will need to find a way to slow down dual-threat quarterback Lincoln Kienholz, who has thrown for 2,739 yards while completing 67.5% of his passes. He has recorded 20 passing touchdowns and four interceptions while also contributing 392 rushing yards and 11 touchdowns on the ground. In total, Kienholz has accounted for 31 touchdowns this season, making him one of the biggest threats Kentucky will have to contain. Louisville also has two talented running backs, with Isaac Brown leading the way. Brown has recorded 120 carries for 834 rushing yards and eight touchdowns. The Cardinals also rely on Keyjuan Brown, who has totaled 96 carries for 672 yards and six touchdowns. At wide receiver, Louisville has several players who contribute to the passing game, but three have emerged as the team’s primary targets. Tre Richardson leads the group with 58 receptions for 822 receiving yards and five touchdowns. Lawayne McCoy has recorded 36 receptions for 640 yards and six touchdowns, while TreyShun Hurry has added 45 receptions for 542 yards and three touchdowns. As mentioned earlier, Louisville has not been particularly strong defensively this season, but there are a few players Kentucky will need to watch closely. Stanquan Clark leads the Cardinals in tackles with 77, making him one of the team’s most important defensive players. Kentucky will need to find ways to avoid him in space and prevent him from making plays. Defensive lineman Tyler Thompson is another player to watch, as he has recorded 6.5 of Louisville’s 32 sacks this season. That means he is responsible for roughly one-fifth of the team’s total sacks, making him a major threat along the defensive line. Kentucky will also need to take care of the football, as turnovers have become a major concern over the past three games. The Wildcats have committed turnovers in every game since their matchup against Tennessee. Kentucky recorded two fumbles and an interception against the Volunteers, one fumble against Florida, and one fumble along with two interceptions against Missouri. Those numbers are concerning, especially considering Kentucky had only five turnovers before that stretch, including three against Alabama and two against South Alabama. Louisville’s defense has recorded 12 interceptions this season, with defensive back Kaleb Beasley responsible for five of them. Kentucky will need to be especially careful when throwing in his direction. The Cardinals have also forced eight fumbles, meaning the Wildcats will need to protect the football and avoid giving Louisville any extra opportunities. If Kentucky hopes to pull off the upset, it will need to play a clean game, limit turnovers, and find a way to slow down Louisville’s explosive offense. How to watch Louisville Cardinals vs. Kentucky Wildcats Location: Kroger Field — Lexington, Kentucky Date: Saturday, November 28 Time: 12:00 p.m. ET Online streaming: WatchESPN Radio: UK Sports Network Opening odds: FanDuel lists Kentucky as a +2.5-point underdog after the Wildcats were previously -1.5-point favorites. ESPN win probability: Kentucky has just a 35.6% chance of winning, according to ESPN . Our early prediction: Before the season started, I predicted Kentucky would win six games but lose to Louisville, believing Will Stein would have too much emotion coaching against his former team, where he once played. While Kentucky is currently on a three-game losing streak and sits at 7-4 on the season, Louisville has won six straight games and is now 8-3. Many believe all the momentum is on Louisville’s side, which makes complete sense, especially since several other outlets are now predicting the Cardinals to defeat Kentucky. The Wildcats will need to finish drives and find a way to slow down Louisville’s high-powered offense. Kentucky has shown throughout the season that it can do that at times, including during matchups against South Carolina and LSU. With all of that being said, I believe this game will mirror the 2023 matchup, when Kentucky escaped with a 38-31 victory on the road. Although this year’s game will be played at Kroger Field, I believe the Wildcats will pull off another victory in a high-scoring contest. Kentucky will close out the regular season with an 8-4 record, solidifying what I believe has been a magnificent first season under Stein. Final score: Kentucky 34, Louisville 27. Tech couple Clemson Given Lackluster Prediction Ahead of South Carolina Showdown (Ken Ruinard / USA Today Network / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images) Matt Levine · Roundtable Sports - Clemson Tue, November 24, 2026 at 11:55 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Clemson Tigers were able to take down the Duke Blue Devils on the road last week, picking up a massive win for the season. Clemson is now 7-4 on the season, with the team having won four of its last six games overall. The Tigers have rebounded nicely from a poor opening part of the season, despite a lackluster offense all year. But as the Tigers prepare for the final week of the regular season, the only focus is on getting a win over the rival South Carolina Gamecocks. Clemson will be hosting South Carolina in the game, giving themselves a slight edge entering the contest. South Carolina will come into the game with a record of 6-5 for the season, coming off two straight blow out losses. The Gamecocks have lost by a score of 34-6 in two straight weeks, and they will try to bounce back this week against Clemson. Both sides understand the rivalry aspect of this game, with the Tigers wanting to add another win to the season's resume. But South Carolina won't go down quietly, looking to spoil the Tigers' final home game of the year. Heading into the game, the Tigers are being viewed as the underdogs, despite having the better record than South Carolina. According to the ESPN matchup predictor , Clemson has a 44.2 percent chance of taking down the Gamecocks this week at home. Quarterback Trent Pearman will likely get the starting nod in this game after leading the Tigers to a win last week. Pearman did well enough for Clemson to win, and it seems that the program wants to see more from him in this game. Overall, Pearman went 17-of-27 for 164 yards, with no touchdown passes against the Blue Devils. But he did rush for 51 yards and a touchdown, showing that he can be a dual-threat option for Clemson. If Pearman can continue to help the offense, it could give Clemson an opportunity to grab the win. Clemson's defense has been strong all year, and South Carolina's offense has been very stagnant over the last few weeks. Clemson head coach Dabo Swinney has been criticized all season long , but if this team could get a win over the Gamecocks, it could go a long way for him. The 2026 season won't be seen as a complete success, but after how it started, the Tigers may end the year on a high note.

Tech couple Former Clemson football safety Khalil Barnes picks off South Carolina Drew Landon, Clemson Wire · Clemson Wire Sun, November 22, 2026 at 3:24 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Khalil Barnes may have traded orange for red and black, but habits from longtime friends are hard to get rid of. The former Clemson football player came down with a late third-quarter interception against rivals South Carolina on Saturday night, ending a Gamecocks red-zone threat and helping top-ranked Georgia hold a 27-6 lead going into the fourth quarter. South Carolina quarterback LaNorris Sellers was driving inside the Georgia 22 when he forced a throw into traffic. Barnes was lingering and waiting. The pick took away South Carolina's best chance to cut into the deficit and handed the ball straight back to the Bulldogs. It was the only turnover of the night for either team at that point and the only one South Carolina couldn't afford at the time. The Gamecocks, ranked 21st at 6-4, had managed just two field goals before the interception. Georgia, 9-1 and ranked first, had already built a two-score cushion behind two Nate Frazier rushing touchdowns and a pair of field goals from Peyton Woodring. For Clemson fans, the sight of Barnes snuffing out a South Carolina drive had to feel familiar probably even a tad bit confusing for the head to digest. He left Death Valley, but nobody let his instincts know that they should do the same. Somewhere in Upstate South Carolina, Tigers fans are watching a former player in a Bulldogs jersey do exactly what they would have asked of him, and deciding whether to be proud or just slightly annoyed that it's happening in another uniform. Barnes may be wearing a Georgia G now, but the Tiger paw is clearly still stamped somewhere in his blood. The Gamecocks will need to regroup quickly if they are to win this one. Georgia leads 27-6 with the fourth quarter just starting up. This was written in the fourth quarter of the Georgia vs. South Carolina game. But national rankings rarely dictate the tempo of this bitter in-state clash. Clemson's Ground Game and Stifling Defense Clemson enters Saturday riding the high of a defensive masterclass. Just days ago, the Tigers walked into Durham as 13.5-point underdogs and dismantled Duke 20-10. The blueprint was simple: control the clock and suffocate the opposition. Clemson's defense allowed just 11 first downs all night, keeping the Blue Devils' offense on the field for a paltry 22 minutes and 45 seconds. By the time Duke regained possession following Chris Denson's 7-yard, fourth-quarter touchdown run, the game was effectively out of reach. Offensively, the Tigers unleashed a punishing, multi-pronged rushing attack. Three different players eclipsed the 50-yard mark, led by Jarvis Green's 84 yards on 16 carries and Denson's 71 yards. The catalyst, however, was Trent Pearman. In his first career start, the quarterback proved poised under pressure. Pearman completed 17 of 27 passes for 164 yards and added 51 yards on the ground. His decisive 9-yard touchdown scramble in the third quarter gave Clemson a lead it never relinquished. Now, he faces a South Carolina defense desperate for a bounce-back performance. Gamecocks Look to Rebound After Georgia Mauling South Carolina arrives in Death Valley needing a win to match Clemson's 7-4 record, but they must first shake off the lingering effects of a brutal 34-6 home loss to No. 1 Georgia. The Gamecocks' primary objective will be jumpstarting quarterback LaNorris Sellers. The top-ranked Bulldogs terrorized Sellers in the pocket, sacking him three times and intercepting him once. He finished the afternoon with just 87 passing yards and 24 rushing yards. If South Carolina is to cover the 5.5-point spread in one of college football's most hostile environments, Sellers will need the time and space that Georgia strictly denied him. Kickoff from Memorial Stadium is scheduled for 3 p.m. ET Saturday on ESPN2. There was confusion galore around South Carolina’s quarterback room last week. Is LaNorris Sellers healthy? Would he be available? Is he going to play? What’s the definition of probable? Does anything anyone says really mean anything? The answer to those questions was that Cutter Woods started at quarterback for South Carolina in its loss to Arkansas. It remains to be seen if Sellers will return from the ankle injury he sustained vs. Texas A&M or if Woods will get the second start of his career. Is all CFP hope lost? South Carolina’s hopes of making the College Football Playoff seemed completely lost after it was upset on the road by Arkansas last week. After all, there’s no way a team with four losses who was just defeated by an unranked team would stick around in the CFP rankings…right? Wrong.
