away.headline: USC suspends entire marching band from UCLA game over crude sign prank on Bruins campus
away.blurb: "Out of respect for UCLA, and to provide time to reflect on the collective responsibility we share to uphold our university's values, the university and Trojan Marching Band's leadership have decided that the band will not take the field for their traditional pre-game and halftime performances at the Rose Bowl this Saturday." USC pulled its marching band from Saturday's rivalry game at the Rose Bowl following a late-night campus prank at UCLA . Ahead of the Big Ten matchup between No. 15 USC and No. 9 UCLA, officials barred the Trojan Marching Band from its pregame and halftime shows after members allegedly vandalized signage at the Wasserman Football Center. The incident capped off a spirited Tuesday night in Los Angeles. An hour after the latest College Football Playoff rankings dropped, USC held its annual Conquest pep rally featuring a mock fight between the USC and UCLA mascots. The marching band performed and several USC players attended. Head coach Lincoln Riley did not make an appearance. Later that night, according to UCLA's Daily Bruin, band members allegedly crossed town and removed letters from the Wasserman Football Center's exterior sign to spell "ass Football Center." The vandalism left the facility temporarily branded as the "ASS Football Center." USC President Beong-Soo Kim responded Wednesday with a formal apology to UCLA. "This morning, we learned that a portion of UCLA's campus had been vandalized by individual students belonging to the Trojan Marching Band. This conduct runs contrary to USC's values and is unacceptable," Kim wrote in a statement to the Trojan community. "We are cooperating fully with law enforcement and an investigation is underway. Appropriate interim actions will be or have already been taken, and any student ultimately found responsible will be subject to discipline under university policy." The move will sideline hundreds of student musicians for the actions of a few. Kim added that the decision was made jointly with band leadership. "We want to express our deepest apologies to the entire UCLA community. Our rivalry is one of the great traditions in college athletics, and it has always rested on mutual respect. What happened on UCLA's campus last night has no place in this tradition," Kim wrote. A USC spokesperson declined to share details on the damages or disciplinary process, telling Fox News Digital. "The university does not have further comment as the investigation into the matter is ongoing." UCLA offered Fox News Digital a much looser response: "Go Bruins. Beat SC!" The Crosstown Showdown has a long history of rivalry week pranks and campus raids. Every November, USC students wrap the Tommy Trojan statue in duct tape to protect it from blue and gold paint, while UCLA students pull overnight shifts guarding the Bruin Bear statue and hiding it under a wooden box. USC and UCLA kick off Saturday afternoon in Pasadena. No "Tusk" blaring from the sidelines. Send us your thoughts: alejandro.avila@outkick.

I thought our edge – some of the things I felt like this team has done pretty consistently throughout the year, I just didn’t see that. “But I was confident that they would respond, and they did.” Adjustments have been made to practice this week in an attempt to eliminate any complacency that could show up in this weekend’s important rivalry game against No. 10 UCLA (10-1, 7-1). “We had some crazy practices already,” cornerback Jontez Williams said with a smirk. “I’d just say we’ve been back to what we need to be, for sure. Tight end Tucker Ashcraft was on the council while playing at Wisconsin, and has now assumed a role with USC’s group. home.headline: USC suspends entire marching band from UCLA game over crude sign prank on Bruins campus
home.blurb: "Out of respect for UCLA, and to provide time to reflect on the collective responsibility we share to uphold our university's values, the university and Trojan Marching Band's leadership have decided that the band will not take the field for their traditional pre-game and halftime performances at the Rose Bowl this Saturday." USC pulled its marching band from Saturday's rivalry game at the Rose Bowl following a late-night campus prank at UCLA . Ahead of the Big Ten matchup between No. 15 USC and No. 9 UCLA, officials barred the Trojan Marching Band from its pregame and halftime shows after members allegedly vandalized signage at the Wasserman Football Center. The incident capped off a spirited Tuesday night in Los Angeles. An hour after the latest College Football Playoff rankings dropped, USC held its annual Conquest pep rally featuring a mock fight between the USC and UCLA mascots. The marching band performed and several USC players attended. Head coach Lincoln Riley did not make an appearance. Later that night, according to UCLA's Daily Bruin, band members allegedly crossed town and removed letters from the Wasserman Football Center's exterior sign to spell "ass Football Center." The vandalism left the facility temporarily branded as the "ASS Football Center." USC President Beong-Soo Kim responded Wednesday with a formal apology to UCLA. "This morning, we learned that a portion of UCLA's campus had been vandalized by individual students belonging to the Trojan Marching Band. This conduct runs contrary to USC's values and is unacceptable," Kim wrote in a statement to the Trojan community. "We are cooperating fully with law enforcement and an investigation is underway. Appropriate interim actions will be or have already been taken, and any student ultimately found responsible will be subject to discipline under university policy." The move will sideline hundreds of student musicians for the actions of a few. Kim added that the decision was made jointly with band leadership. "We want to express our deepest apologies to the entire UCLA community. Our rivalry is one of the great traditions in college athletics, and it has always rested on mutual respect. What happened on UCLA's campus last night has no place in this tradition," Kim wrote. A USC spokesperson declined to share details on the damages or disciplinary process, telling Fox News Digital. "The university does not have further comment as the investigation into the matter is ongoing." UCLA offered Fox News Digital a much looser response: "Go Bruins. Beat SC!" The Crosstown Showdown has a long history of rivalry week pranks and campus raids. Every November, USC students wrap the Tommy Trojan statue in duct tape to protect it from blue and gold paint, while UCLA students pull overnight shifts guarding the Bruin Bear statue and hiding it under a wooden box. USC and UCLA kick off Saturday afternoon in Pasadena. No "Tusk" blaring from the sidelines. Send us your thoughts: alejandro.avila@outkick.

Tech couple Corbie Craig Contributing writer Tue, November 24, 2026 at 10:55 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads College football rivalry week is here, and some of the toughest teams to price are the ones making changes this late in the season. Oklahoma has won three straight with Jason Witten calling plays, Minnesota just won after changing its offensive coordinator, and Wisconsin got a big performance from a quarterback who had lost his starting job. There are reasons to believe those offenses are improving, but I want to be careful about how much of last Saturday carries into this week. I'm starting with three unders, looking at the way these teams have been moving the ball and how much work it takes them to score. Here are my three early Week 13 bets. No. 19 Oklahoma at No. 24 Missouri (-1.5, 41.5) Oklahoma has looked better since Witten took over. Quarterback John Mateer has settled down, and the offense is giving its defense a chance to rest. I understand why people would expect more points here. Against Ole Miss, all three of Oklahoma's offensive scoring drives took at least 12 plays, and Isaiah Sategna added a punt-return touchdown, which helped turn a game in which Mateer threw for 111 yards into a 24-17 win. Then against Texas A&M, the Sooners were tied entering the fourth quarter before finishing a 15-play touchdown drive that took more than eight minutes. A later interception set up a one-play touchdown to Sategna, making the final score look a lot more comfortable than the game had been. Witten can keep Mateer in manageable situations, use the running game and keep Missouri's offense off the field. Oklahoma's defense has held Florida and Texas A&M to seven points apiece during this stretch, with Ole Miss scoring 17 between them. Missouri will test it. QB Austin Simmons threw four touchdown passes against Kentucky, and WR Donovan Olugbode caught two of them. I'm more concerned about those receivers creating quick scores than Missouri consistently driving the length of the field. The Tigers also allowed Kentucky into the red zone seven times while giving up only 14 points, so their defense gave up more chances than the final score suggests. I expect Oklahoma to stick with the patient approach that has worked under Witten, while making Simmons put together longer drives to score. Bet: Under 41.5 (-110) Minnesota at Wisconsin (-7.5, 37.5) Wisconsin just scored 42 points at Purdue, so this is a pretty low number to come back and bet under. RB Colton Joseph returned to the starting job and ran for 187 yards, including touchdowns from 32 and 66 yards out. Darrion Dupree broke a long touchdown run, too. Purdue couldn't handle the quarterback run game, and Wisconsin kept going back to it. Minnesota has to do a better job there. The Gophers allowed Northwestern to rush for 196 yards, and Joseph gave Wisconsin a way to turn a missed assignment into a touchdown without throwing the ball. That's the biggest concern with this bet — but I still don't trust Minnesota to score much. P.J. Fleck fired offensive coordinator Greg Harbaugh Jr. after the Penn State loss, and Eric Koehler took over the play-calling against Northwestern. Darius Taylor ran the ball better and two missed field goals hurt, but the Gophers still went into halftime scoreless. Their first touchdown required a fourth-down conversion, and Anthony Smith then forced and recovered a fumble to give Minnesota a short field for its second TD. QB Drake Lindsey made a great throw late to set up the winning field goal, but even with those plays, Minnesota finished with only 20 points. It hasn't scored more than that in any of its past six games. I can give the coaching change some credit without expecting everything to be fixed before a trip to Wisconsin. The Badgers' defense ranks No. 21 in our ratings, and neither offense is in much of a hurry between snaps. If Minnesota can make Joseph and Dupree string together first downs instead of breaking long runs, Wisconsin can move the ball while taking plenty of time off the clock. Bet: Under 37.5 (-110) North Dakota State (-9.5, 39.5) at San José State San José State nearly forced overtime against UNLV, but the offense still had to work awfully hard to get to 22 points. QB Luke Weaver threw 40 passes while the Spartans ran for just 56 yards. They needed a late touchdown pass to Carson Clark to get within a 2-point conversion then couldn't complete the tying attempt. A week earlier, they scored three points at Air Force. We still rank this offense 128th, and I'm not convinced Weaver gets enough help from the running game to keep it moving against North Dakota State. The Bison's defense certainly gave us a reason to hesitate last week. They led Northern Illinois 31-3 before allowing touchdowns on the Huskies' final three possessions. I still put more weight on a defense we rank No. 29, which held Hawai'i to 13 points and UTEP to seven in its previous two games. San José State needs to sustain drives against that group, and its past two games haven't given me much confidence it can. QB Nathan Hayes is coming off a career-high four touchdown passes, but the Bison finished Saturday by adding defensive tackles as blockers and handing the ball to DJ Scott to run out the clock. With North Dakota State favored here, I expect it to lean on the running game if it gets ahead. I'll back its defense to keep San José State from turning this into a game Hayes has to win through the air. Bet: Under 39.5 (+100)

away.blurb: A total of eight players appeared on Indiana's Week 12 availability report on Thursday night. Six of those players have already been ruled out for Saturday's contest against the Huskies, and that group includes some key starters. The biggest losses for Indiana come on the offensive side of the ball. RB Turbo Richard and OL Joe Brunner both being unavailable for the second straight week is a tough blow to Indiana's rushing attack. After taking down USC by a score of 27-13 last week, the Indiana Hoosiers are hitting the road in Week 12. Traveling across the country to Seattle, this weekend's tilt against Washington is the furthest road trip of the regular season for IU. For the most part, Indiana has stayed relatively healthy this season. Curt Cignetti has a solid strategy in place to keep his players healthy, which includes prioritizing player recovery, managing practice workloads, and ensuring athletes receive proper rest and conditioning throughout the season. But at the end of the day, this is still football and injuries happen. Heading into Week 12, the Hoosiers are dealing with some injuries to key players that present some challenges against Washington. Indiana Football Week 12 injury report Here's a look at the full availability report for Indiana heading into Week 12: Richard was brought in from Boston College over the offseason to be Indiana's RB1, and he thrived in that role when healthy. Richard has rushed for 745 yards and team-leading 6.6 yards per carry with 6 touchdowns this season. The good news is that Khobie Martin is back after missing the first half of the season with a broken forearm, and he rushed 12 times for 82 yards and a touchdown last week against USC. Lee Beebe Jr. has also been a reliable rushing force this season, and he totaled 71 yards on 16 carries last week against the Trojans. With Richard sidelined, Martin and Beebe figure to share the workload in the Hoosier backfield once again. Brunner is a fifth-year senior who has been a key part of Indiana's offensive line this season. He transferred to Indiana from Wisconsin back in the spring, and brought plenty of experience with him as he appeared in 39 games with 24 starts during his career with the Badgers. Owning a 6'7" 320-pound frame, Brunner started the first nine games of the season at right guard for the Hoosiers. In his absence, redshirt sophomore Austin Liebfried got the starting nod at right guard against USC on Saturday afternoon. He could be expected to continue in that role, but freshman Sam Simpson could also see expanded opportunities. Last week without Richard and Brunner, Indiana ran for 146 yards and 4.2 yards per carry against USC. Washington's run defense isn't the best in the world, as the Huskies rank 10th in the Big Ten by allowing 132.4 rushing yards per game to their opponents. If the Hoosiers can get the ground game rolling early and often, it certainly bodes their chances of finding the win column on the road in a tough environment. No. 8 In

picks.blurb: Four Bold Predictions for Oklahoma State Cowboys vs. Arizona State Sun Devils in Week 12 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football CFP And Bowl Games Steelers release Aaron Rodgers NBA Cup roundup Latest CFP rankings MLB free agency updates Viral Ga. Tech couple Oklahoma State Cowboys head coach Eric Morris. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Matt Postins · Oklahoma State Cowboys On SI Fri, November 20, 2026 at 9:30 PM UTC · 6 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Earlier this week Oklahoma State head coach Eric Morris made it clear his team has something to play for even with the Big 12 title game off the table. He didn't want to hear anything about lower intensity from his Cowboys (6-4, 4-3 in Big 12) as they prepared for a 9:15 p.m. central kickoff against Arizona State (6-4, 4-3) on Saturday. "[That's] such a silly question to ask - what is there left to play? For us, right now, it's building this thing up, and for our players that have fought so hard [finishing this season is important]." The Cowboys are bowl eligible for the first time since 2023. The Sun Devils are bowl eligible for the third year in a row. The winner of this game could end up with a better bowl bid with a victory. As the Cowboys prepare for a late kickoff against the Sun Devils, here are four bold predictions, including the final score. Caleb Hawkins Has 200+ Yards in Total Offense Oklahoma State Cowboys running back Caleb Hawkins. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Arizona State's defense has been better the past few weeks. It's part of the reason the Sun Devils have won three of their last four games. In that span, they've given up fewer than 17 points three times and allowed 27 points to BYU in the one loss. Arizona State has figured some things out and Morris noted that the Sun Devils have stopped the run well of late. The Cowboys have featured Caleb Hawkins in a big way the last five games. He's rushed for 648 yards and five touchdowns and caught 32 passes for 401 yards and three touchdowns. That's 1,049 all-purpose yards in five games. He's second in the country in the category. Oklahoma State wants to feature him. More important, given Drew Mestemaker's shoulder injury, the Cowboys NEED to feature him. He got 26 touches against Texas Tech and had 143 yards without a score. I suspect the Cowboys are going to feed him in the run game early to allow Mestemaker to settle in - I expected him to start - and then get him the ball in space in the pass game once Mestemaker is comfortably. The Cowboys need him to get 200 or more yards in total offense on Saturday. I think he gets it. Broderick Vehrs Plays a Role on Offense Oklahoma State Cowboys quarterback Broderick Vehrs. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect As I just wrote, I expect Drew Mestemaker to start at quarterback. But it doesn't mean that head coach Eric Morris can't use Broderick Vehrs in some way. He's likely gotten some first-team reps this week on the off-chance that Mestemaker can't go. That has given Morris a chance to look at ways to use the true freshman in ways that could lessen Mestemaker's load and reduce his exposure to injury. Morris has gotten creative with the playbook at times. A couple of weeks ago he ran a play-action shovel pass that happened so quickly I'm not sure anyone realized it. There is little Morris can do if Mestemaker gets flushed out of the pocket. But he won't want to use Mestemaker in designed runs. That's where Vehrs can come in handy. He's shown an ability to run the ball in RPO looks that could help throw defenses off in the right circumstance. He has 58 yards rushing on just five carries so there is some explosiveness there. How Morris uses Vehrs will depend on comfort level. But a package that allows him a handful of plays to try and throw off Arizona State's defense would have the added benefit of minimizing Mestemaker's exposure to re-injury. The Cowboys Get a Defensive Touchdown OSU safety Evan Jackson. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect It's time. In fact, it's past time for the Oklahoma State Cowboys to land another defensive touchdown. It's Game 11. It's time for someone to find the end zone the same way safety Evan Jackson did against UCF. Why should the offense have all the fun? But why this week? The Sun Devils moved to true freshman quarterback Jake Fette as the starter three games ago and he's had a similar impact on Arizona State as veteran quarterback Thomas Castelllanos has had on Texas Tech. He's thrown for 623 yards and three touchdowns with no interceptions. He's also rushed for 23 yards. He hasn't committed a turnover ... yet. Fette will be without one of his top wide receivers, Omarion Miller, who has caught 49 passes this season. He played last week against UCF, so Fette hasn't had the chance to play without the team's second-highest producing receiver. That takes away a rock-solid target. The Cowboys will also be looking for redemption defensively after giving up 52 points to the Red Raiders. Remember how Oklahoma State answered after giving up 51 points to Iowa State? The Cowboys allowed 28 points to Kansas State and forced three turnovers. That's the kind of bounce-back I'm expecting from the Cowboys this Saturday. That bounce-back will lead to a turnover that leads to a defensive touchdown. Given his hard work the past two months, I'll take the easy way out and say LaDainian Fields ends up with a pick-six. Score Prediction Oklahoma State Cowboys quarterback Drew Mestemaker. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Oklahoma State 37, Arizona State 33 The Cowboys haven't been great on the road this season. The performances have been uneven and they're 2-3 away from BPS. But Oklahoma State has followed up every loss with a win this season and I think that's what happens on Saturday. I think quarterback Drew Mestemaker plays without restrictions, but that running back Caleb Hawkins ends up being the star of the show. The defense frustrates ASU quarterback Jake Fette just enough to force him into his first significant mistakes of the season. Cowboys kicker Sam Keltner boots a career-long field goal in the thinner air of Tempe. After that, Oklahoma State will fly home for the regular-season finale against Kansas and awaits its bowl game invitation.
